grading_policy: Every requested material part separately; equivalent wording accepted, unasked extra details not demanded, no borrowing facts between answers. Confidence labels ignored.
benchmark_validity: SUPERSEDED: later essential defense-source gap recorded. Historical fixed-key recovery counts do not establish a complete core PASS.

grades.question: During attrition, how does an office roll resolve, what extra modifier does the Chairman have, and where do a retiring member, card and fatigue go?
grades.expected_answer: Roll separately per office card, +1 per fatigue and an additional +1 for Chairman. 1–2 nothing, 3–4 add fatigue, 5+ retire: member to Pensioners, card flipped into Vacant Offices, fatigue returned to supply.
grades.observed_answer: For each held office card, roll one die simultaneously, add one per fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. A modified result of 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the officeholder. A retiree moves to Pensioners, the card is flipped into Vacant Offices, and its fatigue is returned to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal office attrition rolls.
grades.reason: Attrition thresholds, per-fatigue and Chairman modifiers, and pensioner/card/fatigue destinations are all explicit.

grades.question: Who may select London Season cards, in what order and with which tiebreakers? What happens to the display and unused pensioners afterward?
grades.expected_answer: Each player retiring at least one pensioner must take or discard one display card, descending actual total retirement spending; ties most total windows then PM clockwise order. May peek at display blackmails. Stop when display empty. Discard remaining display and refill three, blackmail down/prestige up even if none taken. Return unretired pensioners to supply.
grades.observed_answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending; ties go to the player with the most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. A selected or discarded card is not replaced during selection; if the display empties, every remaining eligible player is skipped. At the end, discard all cards left in the display and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.
grades.reason: Eligibility, actual spending order, both tiebreakers, take/discard, no immediate replacement, empty-display skip, faceup/down refill and pensioner return are resolved.

grades.question: How do the opportunity marker and extra-action laws affect family actions? If four offices are vacant and the marker already sits on Enlist Writer, how many writers can be placed?
grades.expected_answer: Normal selected action once, or twice if marker already there at phase start; move marker to main action. Only latest passed extra-action law usable, extra action gets no marker doubling and does not move marker. Four or more vacancies allow one extra writer once per turn, so repeated Enlist Writer can place three total.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of a player's Family phase action, check where their opportunity marker was at phase start. They choose a main family action once, or twice if the marker already matched that action, and then place or move the marker onto the chosen action. After that main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is never doubled by the marker and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action can place two writers, and the four-vacancy rule adds one additional writer once this turn, for three writers total.
grades.summary_evidence: Family phase procedure; Enlist Writer row
grades.reason: Ordinary main action, phase-start matching/doubling, marker movement, latest extra law without marker effects and three-writer once-per-turn bonus are resolved.

grades.question: After Seek Share actions, how are new Company shares created and remaining applicants moved? Where was the initial purchase money paid?
grades.expected_answer: Seek Share pays printed empty Stock Exchange space price to bank. At end Family, while Debt and applicants remain, move rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt one per share. With no Debt, shift remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Money does not enter Company treasury.
grades.observed_answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide all remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The money paid when seeking a share goes to the bank; it is not paid into Company treasuries.
grades.summary_evidence: New Company shares; Seek Share row
grades.reason: Rightmost-first issue while Debt exists, one Debt reduction per share, order-preserving shift and bank payment destination are all supplied.

grades.question: When hiring, how are vacancies ordered, what consent does hiring your own family require, what happens to promoted fatigue, and what if no candidate or hirer exists?
grades.expected_answer: Ascending back-of-card office numbers, insert promotion vacancy in ascending order; own-family hiring needs verbal consent of every other player represented in candidate pool, except Chairman election. Promoted fatigue travels to new card. No candidate or vacant hiring office means skip office; remains vacant and takes no actions including hiring.
grades.observed_answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the backs of their cards. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that family member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. For an ordinary office hire involving the hirer's own family, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
grades.reason: The ordinary own-family rule is given but the Chairman-election exception is omitted. This exception was treated as material consistently in prior independent adjudications; Q006 cannot supply it.

grades.question: How is a Chairman elected, how does a deadlocked election resolve, and does the elected Chairman piece remain a tradable Company share?
grades.expected_answer: Candidate must own share, needs consent of players controlling pure majority (>half) current shares; first to achieve support elected. Deadlock former Chairman picks any shareholder including self without Nepotism. Winner moves one share into Chairman slot; still share but cannot trade it or use it for firm investment.
grades.observed_answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares constitute a pure majority, meaning more than half of the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody gets the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority calculations, and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
grades.reason: Pure-majority shareholder election, deadlock former-Chairman choice including self without Nepotism, and continuing untradable/noninvestable share status are supplied.

grades.question: Explain success-check results, payment, retries, catastrophic destinations and the restriction against dead actions.
grades.expected_answer: Commit office treasury money/resources, gather dice then subtract penalty; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure retry if sufficient resources, 5–6 catastrophe: no more office actions, officeholder to supply, card flipped to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply (specific office exceptions apply). No action without effect or chance of success.
grades.observed_answer: Before a Company-office success check, commit its resources and any cash; all cash for that check comes from the acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to the supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading without a ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.
grades.reason: Acting-office cash paid to bank, resources minus penalty, lowest-die results/retries, catastrophic destinations and no-dead-action rule are explicit.

grades.question: What are the Chairman’s voluntary borrowing and allocation duties, including consent and track limits?
grades.expected_answer: May advance Debt three times freely, +£5 Balance each. Each further advancement needs majority-shareholder consent including Chairman share; cannot pass Debt track end. Must allocate all Company Balance to other office treasuries, reducing Balance accordingly; borrowing may interleave allocation while respecting limit.
grades.observed_answer: The Chairman may take up to three Debt advances freely, adding £5 to Balance for each, but may never advance past the Debt track end. Each additional advance beyond three requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, subject to the borrowing limits; cash already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.
grades.reason: Three free £5 advances, further majority consent including Chairman, track limit, all-Balance allocation and allowed interleaving are resolved.

grades.question: What must Shipping do with its budget? State ship costs, destinations, consent requirements and the prerequisite for buying Company ships.
grades.expected_answer: Spend until at most £2 remains. Lease extra £2, fit shipyard ship £3 without owner consent, buy Company £5 only with no ships remaining on shipyards. Place acquired ships in any sea zone (China eligible once created). Extras return at Refresh.
grades.observed_answer: Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Extra ships remain only until Refresh.
grades.reason: Mandatory spending endpoint, all three costs, shipyard consent waiver, Company-ship prerequisite and sea-zone destinations are supplied.

grades.question: For a President’s Trade action, explain declared regions, dice penalty, routes and capacity, insufficient writers, protected home regions, bonuses and successful-trade limit.
grades.expected_answer: Declare home plus only actually reachable regions with sufficient ships and open route; £1 per die minus one per nonhome declared region. Success fill as many orders as possible in declared regions, one per ship, first home port then adjacent own placed writers. Use filled tokens if writers exhausted. Cannot fill another Presidency home region even vacant. Company receives printed order values, President £1 per filled order, writer owner £1 per writer placed; at most one successful trade per President per turn. Revenue exception: under Deregulation an order already filled by a firm this turn pays the Company half listed value, rounded down; President and writer bonuses remain unchanged.
grades.observed_answer: For Trade, declare regions including the Presidency's home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failure may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; at most one successful Trade per President per turn, and catastrophe removes the President. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. Place the first actual writer at the home port; each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another Presidency's home region, even if that other office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it that turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and owners receive £1 per writer placed. Use dividers to separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies for Refresh.
grades.source_references: Rules pp20–21; lines 1540–1582; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Home/reachable declarations, dice penalties, connected home-first capacity and token substitution, protected home regions, personal bonuses and one successful Trade are explicit; half-value firm-refill exception is included.

grades.question: What can a Commander target with Deploy, what produces dice and penalties, and when and how are officer losses checked?
grades.expected_answer: Target home, associated region or bordering associated region; exclude another home or another Presidency Company region. Own Company target requires closed order/unrest. Exhaust active officers/regiments for one die each, alliances for printed strength, subtract the combined strength of target and all OTHER regions in its empire (target counted once); Company-controlled defending strength zero. After every attempt roll per exhausted officer, each 6 removes an officer to its owner supply, never regiment.
grades.observed_answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with it, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region is a legal target only if it has unrest or a closed order that the action can affect. Exhausted officers and regiments each provide one die; local alliances provide their printed number of dice, and their strength can be used only once that turn for Deploy or defense and cannot be split. Subtract the target's strength plus all other regions in its empire, counting the target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.
grades.source_references: Rules p22; lines 1617–1650; Rules p22 lines1639–1645; p7 lines707–711
grades.reason: All target permissions/exclusions, own-Company effect requirement, resource dice, target-counted-once empire penalty and zero Company strength, and per-attempt officer-six losses are given.

grades.question: On successful Deploy how are loot and trophies calculated and control imposed? What changes if Deploy catastrophically fails?
grades.expected_answer: Loot £4 per tower plus faceup loot modifier, at least surviving used officers+1. Pay Commander £1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer, clockwise other officers, then £1 bank per regiment/alliance piece; repeat until empty. Commander trophy per tower; remove tower/dome, capital matching flags, clear unrest/open all orders. Newly conquer: loot token region-side above President, Governor overlay placed in conquered region and ONLY office card to Vacant Offices stack, Company control; inward redirect Elephant if formerly poised outward there. Catastrophe loses half trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; still check exhausted officer losses.
grades.observed_answer: After a successful Deploy, take loot equal to £4 per target tower plus its faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the surviving participating officers in this attempt plus one. Distribute each payout cycle in order: £1 for the Commander and £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer for other families clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed or the cash runs out. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome, and all matching empire flags if it was a capital; open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not already Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President's box and put the Governor overlay on the conquered region, sending only the office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring. Do not create Governors/overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in the conquered region and faced outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, return half the Commander's family's trophies rounded up and return the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
grades.summary_evidence: Commanders and Deploy; Successful control procedure; catastrophe rule
grades.reason: Loot formula/minimum, clockwise repeating payout and bank pieces, trophies, capital/Elephant cleanup, new Governorship destinations and catastrophic trophy/member/loss effects are resolved.

grades.question: How does Governor Administer work across repeated attempts, including bonuses, tax unrest and stopping?
grades.expected_answer: Start printed dice pool; roll pool, no penalty, lose one die after any attempt. Success £1 bonus, extra £1 if preceding roll failed, choose build Company ship in two successful stages, regiment in associated army, or unsplit £2 Balance/President treasury. Tax after first in turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful check adds unrest. May repeat until stop, pool exhausted or catastrophe (general vacancy rule).
grades.observed_answer: The Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces that pool by one regardless of the result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one benefit: Build, Commission a regiment, or Tax. Build takes two successful Build actions: first put a partially built Company ship in the Governor's region if none is there, then on a later successful Build complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. Commission puts a regiment in that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking dice pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.
grades.reason: Diminishing pool and result-independent decrement, immediate-previous-failure bonus, two separate Build stages/destinations, associated Army, unsplit Tax/unrest and stop conditions are resolved.

grades.question: If Company revenue cannot cover expenses, how do emergency loans work at and below max Debt, how does Standing change, and when are expectations and dividends checked?
grades.expected_answer: Expenses £1 per current Debt, officer/regiment excluding Commander, ship in sea zones including China. Emergency loans +£5 each, advance Debt if possible even at maximum continue borrowing; added Debt costs no current-turn interest, then Balance zero. 1–2 emergency loans Standing -1; 3+ -2. Then compare Balance with expectations at current Standing, if below Standing -1. Then optional dividends £1 per share incl Chairman; total dividend payout strictly greater than expectations advances Standing once. Immediate failure when Standing reaches failure.
grades.observed_answer: Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one per loan until the Debt track ends, and continue taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt does not add an expense this turn. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing; if below expectations, lower Standing one. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing one cash per Company share per dividend and paying £1 per share to each owner including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one. Reaching the leftmost Standing space causes Company failure.
grades.reason: Loan amount/track-cap/no-current-turn-interest, zero Balance, Standing loan bands, current expectations next, optional dividends and strict enthusiasm inequality are supplied; unasked expense/dividend formulas are not required.

grades.question: When Company regions face a Crisis, which regions are attacked, in what order and at what strength? How is defense mounted and what happens on successful defense?
grades.expected_answer: Resolve primary first then all other Company regions with unrest, Bombay/Madras/Bengal Army order; each Commander orders own regions. Primary normal invasion/rebellion strength + local unrest, secondary unrest only. Exhaust newly active Army strength equal attack or as much as possible; insufficient means Region Loss. Successful defense clears unrest and Commander gains trophy. Vacant Commander replaced by Military Affairs then Chairman, acting substitute gains/loses no trophies. Additionally, if the primary Crisis was a normal Invasion which failed against the Company, remove one tower level from the attacker if possible.
grades.observed_answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency, its Commander orders the attacks. A normal primary Crisis attack strength is its ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. For a primary Foreign Invasion, use only the ordinary attack die, without added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the unrest cubes in that region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If the newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, perform Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in the attacked region and give the Commander one trophy; if this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gets or loses no trophies. A successful primary Invasion against the Company also applies empire growth.
grades.source_references: Rules p33; lines 2262–2296; Rules p33 lines2290–2296
grades.reason: Historical frozen key: primary-first and Presidency/Commander order, unrest-only secondaries, primary strength, compulsory defense and vacant substitutes, trophy/unrest cleanup and failed-primary-Invasion attacker tower loss are supplied. Subsequent source-gap discovery invalidates any complete core signoff for excess alliance strength.
grades.source_completeness_warning: Historical key did not settle an indivisible alliance exceeding attack strength. Correct means recovery of the historical asked/known procedure only; no definitive overshoot ruling or complete core PASS.

grades.question: What happens when a law fails versus passes, including support-zero, policy movement, Prime Minister and effect order?
grades.expected_answer: Support -1 or lower fails; discard and resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader returns marker and becomes PM, moves selected policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. Zero or higher passes: law with passed laws, PM gains token, selected policy consequence then immediate law effects. Restore vote cards. If legislation fails Company, finish vote then final scoring.
grades.observed_answer: After voting, support of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, return the Opposition Leader's token and give them the PM dial. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support of zero or more passes: place the law with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then resolve immediate law effects. In either outcome, finally restore every voting card to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
grades.reason: Negative failure versus zero-or-positive passage, law/dilemma handling, PM transfer/adjacent policy, policy-before-immediate-law order, vote-card restoration and finish-vote failure timing are supplied.

grades.question: When can or must a Deregulation session be called in the relevant scenarios, and what are its success/failure effects and exceptions from ordinary voting?
grades.expected_answer: 1758/Long1710 start-turn before London: PM may if Standing and/or Debt lined, must if either starred. Pass reduce Debt one per two Debt, Standing to S, PM law token, activate deregulation. Failure raise share VP value up to ±3, law kept, PM stays. No policy and PM may vote against.
grades.observed_answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, with the listed exceptions: there is no policy accompanying the law; a failed vote does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. On passage, lower Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to the maximum of ±3. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated.
grades.reason: Correct scenarios/before-London timing, lined/starred triggers, both outcomes, share-value cap and all special voting exceptions are resolved.

grades.question: How can a firm be formed or invested in, where does money come from, and what restrictions apply to Company shares, invested workshops and the ten-share limit?
grades.expected_answer: Nonmanager forms by returning eligible Company share or flipping workshop invested; flip own board, create family firm share, value leftmost, £5 bank to London. Later investment manager consent, same share/workshop payment gives £5 London and new share. Weak Company share when Standing/Debt lined prohibited; same-turn share prohibited even traded; Chairman piece unavailable. Invested workshop no bonus/failure VP. Ten-share cap but investments continue without new shares.
grades.observed_answer: To form a firm, a player who currently manages no firm returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board, places a family member as the first firm share, sets the value cube to the track's leftmost space, and takes £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and contribute an eligible Company share or workshop; this creates one firm share and sends £5 from the bank to London. A firm may have at most ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be used, and Company shares cannot be invested at all when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. A share created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested status, give no workshop bonus and no Company-failure VP, and remain invested even if the firm fails.
grades.reason: Nonmanager formation and manager-consented investment, eligible share/workshop contributions and £5 bank-to-London funds, initial share/value, weak/immature/Chairman restrictions and permanent workshop/ten-share effects are supplied.

grades.question: Explain firm trading strategy, when checks and order filling occur, initiative, capacity, repeat-filled revenue and firm value growth.
grades.expected_answer: After investments managers secretly choose home/sea zone and London cash bid; need ship, may choose even closed home. Reveal cash but not strategy. At associated Presidency start reveal/check once with bid dice, pay bank. Success initiative ships minus number of 1/2 dice; President successful Trade gets same calculation. Fill lowest initiative first, President breaks ties; absent/nontrading President wait for Commander/Governors and Chairman breaks ties. Firm fills max ships+1 open connected orders from chosen home once each; prior-fill by others allowed for half listed value rounded down. Revenue India, advance value one space per £6 revenue this turn. Company may also fill orders previously filled by firms this turn at half listed value, rounded down, retaining normal President and writer bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port, requiring at least one ship, and secretly bid cash from London treasury; a closed home port is allowed when choosing. Alternatively, choose Hobnob: no bid, trade, or dividends, but still pay expenses and retain the previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously, while strategy cards stay facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's operations, before other actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 allows trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. The President's successful Trade produces initiative the same way. After that success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President chooses order among ties, and the Company does not automatically go first. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after the Commander/Governors have had a chance, with Chairman choosing initiative ties. Each firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting from its home port and tracing its own connected filled route; it fills each particular order at most once. Firms may refill orders filled by others/the Company this turn, and the Company may refill a firm's orders. A previously filled order pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.
grades.source_references: Rules p40; lines 2773–2822; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Secret strategy and public-bid/private-card timing, closed-home and single-attempt constraints, check/payment and initiative, both tie authorities/timing, ships-plus-one route and one fill per order, reciprocal half-revenue refills and £6 India-based value growth are resolved.

grades.question: How are firm expenses and dividends funded and calculated, and what happens to a failing firm, its shares and workshops?
grades.expected_answer: Start Revenue firms act initiative order then others, ties manager windows then PM clockwise. Expenses £1 per ship plus max(shares, firm value); either treasury. If cannot pay dissolution (or emergency rescue): shares Debtors Prison -1 VP each, ships shipyards, charter family, invested workshops stay invested. Dividends only India, £1 per share plus £1 manager each; shareholder may forgo with manager consent. Record total paid retirement marker then sweep remainder India to London.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, before Company revenue, firms pay expenses in initiative order, with ties resolved by managers' most windows and then PM clockwise order. The firm pays £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or firm value, using either or both treasuries. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India treasury; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. With the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid out on the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London. If the firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison at −1 VP each, returns ships to shipyards, returns the charter to the family side, and leaves workshops invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop rules (even if the ten-share cap prevents more shares): pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one per emergency investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if unpaid and cover the failing firm's unpaid expenses.
grades.reason: Expense formula and either treasury, India-only per-share/manager dividends and waiver, actual payout marker/cash sweep, failure/rescue and prison/ship/charter/workshop destinations are supplied; unasked inter-firm order details are not required.

grades.question: During attrition, how does an office roll resolve, what extra modifier does the Chairman have, and where do a retiring member, card and fatigue go?
grades.expected_answer: Roll separately per office card, +1 per fatigue and an additional +1 for Chairman. 1–2 nothing, 3–4 add fatigue, 5+ retire: member to Pensioners, card flipped into Vacant Offices, fatigue returned to supply.
grades.observed_answer: In London Season attrition, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card, add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. Modified 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5 or more retires the officeholder. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return that card's fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make this normal attrition roll.
grades.reason: Attrition thresholds, per-fatigue and Chairman modifiers, and pensioner/card/fatigue destinations are all explicit.

grades.question: Who may select London Season cards, in what order and with which tiebreakers? What happens to the display and unused pensioners afterward?
grades.expected_answer: Each player retiring at least one pensioner must take or discard one display card, descending actual total retirement spending; ties most total windows then PM clockwise order. May peek at display blackmails. Stop when display empty. Discard remaining display and refill three, blackmail down/prestige up even if none taken. Return unretired pensioners to supply.
grades.observed_answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may each take or discard one card from the London Season display. Select in descending order of actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with more total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace a selected or discarded card during selection; if the display empties, immediately skip every remaining eligible player. At the end discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three cards: prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody took a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies; unused pensioners do not carry over.
grades.reason: Eligibility, actual spending order, both tiebreakers, take/discard, no immediate replacement, empty-display skip, faceup/down refill and pensioner return are resolved.

grades.question: How do the opportunity marker and extra-action laws affect family actions? If four offices are vacant and the marker already sits on Enlist Writer, how many writers can be placed?
grades.expected_answer: Normal selected action once, or twice if marker already there at phase start; move marker to main action. Only latest passed extra-action law usable, extra action gets no marker doubling and does not move marker. Four or more vacancies allow one extra writer once per turn, so repeated Enlist Writer can place three total.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of the Family phase, check the opportunity marker's location; a main action may be taken twice only if the marker already matched that chosen action at phase start. After choosing, place or move the marker onto that action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may then grant an extra action; that extra action is not doubled and does not move the marker. Enlist Writer places a member in any Presidency's Writers box. If at least four offices are vacant, it adds one additional writer once that turn. With the marker already on Enlist Writer and four vacant offices, the doubled main action can place two writers plus the one-time extra writer, three writers total.
grades.summary_evidence: Family phase; Family action — Enlist Writer
grades.reason: Ordinary main action, phase-start matching/doubling, marker movement, latest extra law without marker effects and three-writer once-per-turn bonus are resolved.

grades.question: After Seek Share actions, how are new Company shares created and remaining applicants moved? Where was the initial purchase money paid?
grades.expected_answer: Seek Share pays printed empty Stock Exchange space price to bank. At end Family, while Debt and applicants remain, move rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt one per share. With no Debt, shift remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Money does not enter Company treasury.
grades.observed_answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant from the Stock Exchange queue into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Applicants moved to Court are then Company shares. If Debt is exhausted while applicants remain, slide those applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share requires paying its printed queue-space cost to the bank; the initial purchase money does not go to Company treasuries.
grades.summary_evidence: Family action — Seek Share; New Company shares
grades.reason: Rightmost-first issue while Debt exists, one Debt reduction per share, order-preserving shift and bank payment destination are all supplied.

grades.question: When hiring, how are vacancies ordered, what consent does hiring your own family require, what happens to promoted fatigue, and what if no candidate or hirer exists?
grades.expected_answer: Ascending back-of-card office numbers, insert promotion vacancy in ascending order; own-family hiring needs verbal consent of every other player represented in candidate pool, except Chairman election. Promoted fatigue travels to new card. No candidate or vacant hiring office means skip office; remains vacant and takes no actions including hiring.
grades.observed_answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the back of each office card. The designated hirer chooses a candidate, who moves into the office, and that member's owner receives the office card. For an ordinary hire of a member from the hirer's own family, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, move their fatigue to the new office card and insert their old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt from Nepotism and use their own rules.
grades.reason: Ascending vacancies, promotion insertion/fatigue, all represented-family consent with Chairman/Commander exceptions, and absent-candidate/hirer skipping are explicit.

grades.question: How is a Chairman elected, how does a deadlocked election resolve, and does the elected Chairman piece remain a tradable Company share?
grades.expected_answer: Candidate must own share, needs consent of players controlling pure majority (>half) current shares; first to achieve support elected. Deadlock former Chairman picks any shareholder including self without Nepotism. Winner moves one share into Chairman slot; still share but cannot trade it or use it for firm investment.
grades.observed_answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of current shares. Any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. That piece still counts as a share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm. If nobody receives majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, as a fallback; Nepotism consent is not required. If Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns, placing a member from supply or, if needed and possible, from a prize (losing that prize's VP); if this is impossible, there is no Chairman.
grades.reason: Pure-majority shareholder election, deadlock former-Chairman choice including self without Nepotism, and continuing untradable/noninvestable share status are supplied.

grades.question: Explain success-check results, payment, retries, catastrophic destinations and the restriction against dead actions.
grades.expected_answer: Commit office treasury money/resources, gather dice then subtract penalty; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure retry if sufficient resources, 5–6 catastrophe: no more office actions, officeholder to supply, card flipped to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply (specific office exceptions apply). No action without effect or chance of success.
grades.observed_answer: For a Company-office success check, first commit resources and pay any check cash from the acting office's treasury to the bank, gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures modify this general procedure. Do not take a dead action that has no effect or chance of success—for example, trading with no ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses. The summary specifies no generic destination for resources committed to an attempt beyond paying Company-office check cash to the bank; office-specific procedures govern other outcomes.
grades.reason: Acting-office cash paid to bank, resources minus penalty, lowest-die results/retries, catastrophic destinations and no-dead-action rule are explicit.

grades.question: What are the Chairman’s voluntary borrowing and allocation duties, including consent and track limits?
grades.expected_answer: May advance Debt three times freely, +£5 Balance each. Each further advancement needs majority-shareholder consent including Chairman share; cannot pass Debt track end. Must allocate all Company Balance to other office treasuries, reducing Balance accordingly; borrowing may interleave allocation while respecting limit.
grades.observed_answer: The Chairman may borrow up to three Debt freely, adding £5 to Company Balance for each Debt. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and borrowing cannot pass the end of the Debt track. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; money already in office treasuries stays there for those offices. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, subject to the same borrowing limits and consent.
grades.reason: Three free £5 advances, further majority consent including Chairman, track limit, all-Balance allocation and allowed interleaving are resolved.

grades.question: What must Shipping do with its budget? State ship costs, destinations, consent requirements and the prerequisite for buying Company ships.
grades.expected_answer: Spend until at most £2 remains. Lease extra £2, fit shipyard ship £3 without owner consent, buy Company £5 only with no ships remaining on shipyards. Place acquired ships in any sea zone (China eligible once created). Extras return at Refresh.
grades.observed_answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend the office treasury until £2 or less remains. Available purchases are: lease an extra ship for £2; fit a ship from a shipyard for £3, without the shipyard owner's consent; or buy a Company ship for £5, but only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh. The summary does not specify a separate consent requirement for leasing or buying Company ships; owner consent is specifically waived for fitting a ship from a shipyard.
grades.reason: Mandatory spending endpoint, all three costs, shipyard consent waiver, Company-ship prerequisite and sea-zone destinations are supplied.

grades.question: For a President’s Trade action, explain declared regions, dice penalty, routes and capacity, insufficient writers, protected home regions, bonuses and successful-trade limit.
grades.expected_answer: Declare home plus only actually reachable regions with sufficient ships and open route; £1 per die minus one per nonhome declared region. Success fill as many orders as possible in declared regions, one per ship, first home port then adjacent own placed writers. Use filled tokens if writers exhausted. Cannot fill another Presidency home region even vacant. Company receives printed order values, President £1 per filled order, writer owner £1 per writer placed; at most one successful trade per President per turn. Revenue exception: under Deregulation an order already filled by a firm this turn pays the Company half listed value, rounded down; President and writer bonuses remain unchanged.
grades.observed_answer: The President declares Trade regions including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die for every declared nonhome region, then roll the normal check. Failures may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; catastrophe removes the President. A President may have at most one successful Trade per turn. It must allow its Commander, Governors, and Trade their opportunities, and each position completes all actions before another begins; Trade may be ordered before or after the other positions but cannot interrupt one. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within declared regions. The first writer goes to the home port; each subsequent order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President may not fill another Presidency's home region, even if that other President's office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed revenue, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under Deregulation. The President gets £1 from the bank per order and each owner gets £1 per writer placed. Adjacent writers from different Presidencies are separated with dividers for return at Refresh.
grades.source_references: Rules pp20–21; lines 1540–1582; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Home/reachable declarations, dice penalties, connected home-first capacity and token substitution, protected home regions, personal bonuses and one successful Trade are explicit; half-value firm-refill exception is included.

grades.question: What can a Commander target with Deploy, what produces dice and penalties, and when and how are officer losses checked?
grades.expected_answer: Target home, associated region or bordering associated region; exclude another home or another Presidency Company region. Own Company target requires closed order/unrest. Exhaust active officers/regiments for one die each, alliances for printed strength, subtract the combined strength of target and all OTHER regions in its empire (target counted once); Company-controlled defending strength zero. After every attempt roll per exhausted officer, each 6 removes an officer to its owner supply, never regiment.
grades.observed_answer: A Commander may target their Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company-controlled target must have unrest or a closed order, so the Deploy can have an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once, while Company-controlled defense strength is zero. Roll the normal check; a noncatastrophic failure can be retried with remaining resources. After every attempt, the owners roll one die for each officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for losses. A catastrophic failure returns the Commander to supply and returns half that family's trophies rounded up; exhausted officers still check losses, and no office card is vacated because Commanders have none.
grades.source_references: Rules p22; lines 1617–1650; Rules p22 lines1639–1645; p7 lines707–711
grades.reason: All target permissions/exclusions, own-Company effect requirement, resource dice, target-counted-once empire penalty and zero Company strength, and per-attempt officer-six losses are given.

grades.question: On successful Deploy how are loot and trophies calculated and control imposed? What changes if Deploy catastrophically fails?
grades.expected_answer: Loot £4 per tower plus faceup loot modifier, at least surviving used officers+1. Pay Commander £1 plus £1 per own used surviving officer, clockwise other officers, then £1 bank per regiment/alliance piece; repeat until empty. Commander trophy per tower; remove tower/dome, capital matching flags, clear unrest/open all orders. Newly conquer: loot token region-side above President, Governor overlay placed in conquered region and ONLY office card to Vacant Offices stack, Company control; inward redirect Elephant if formerly poised outward there. Catastrophe loses half trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; still check exhausted officer losses.
grades.observed_answer: On a successful Deploy, loot from the bank is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of the number of surviving officers used in this attempt plus one. Count only participating officers who survived this attempt and the regiments and alliance pieces used in it. Distribute each payout cycle in order: £1 to the Commander's family for the Commander plus £1 per their surviving used officer; then £1 per surviving used officer to other families clockwise; then £1 to the bank per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece, regardless of alliance strength. Stop a cycle when the cash runs out, then repeat the entire cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome; if it was an empire capital, remove all matching empire flags. Open all orders and remove all unrest there. If the target was not already Company-controlled, create a Governorship by placing its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President's box, placing the Governor overlay on the map in the conquered region, and sending only the office card to Vacant Offices for later Hiring. Do not create Governors or overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in that conquered region facing outward, move it fully inside, threatening Rebellion. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
grades.summary_evidence: Commanders and Deploy — success payout/control; catastrophe
grades.reason: Loot formula/minimum, clockwise repeating payout and bank pieces, trophies, capital/Elephant cleanup, new Governorship destinations and catastrophic trophy/member/loss effects are resolved.

grades.question: How does Governor Administer work across repeated attempts, including bonuses, tax unrest and stopping?
grades.expected_answer: Start printed dice pool; roll pool, no penalty, lose one die after any attempt. Success £1 bonus, extra £1 if preceding roll failed, choose build Company ship in two successful stages, regiment in associated army, or unsplit £2 Balance/President treasury. Tax after first in turn adds unrest. Any unsuccessful check adds unrest. May repeat until stop, pool exhausted or catastrophe (general vacancy rule).
grades.observed_answer: A Governor starts with the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one benefit: Build a Company ship, Commission a regiment, or Tax. Building takes two successful Build actions: if there is no partially built ship in the region, place one there; otherwise complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. A partially built ship has no other effect. Commissioning places a regiment in that President's Army; it has officer-like strength, pays loot to the bank, and does not roll for officer losses. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful attempt adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking dice pool until the Governor stops, has no dice remaining, or catastrophically fails.
grades.reason: Diminishing pool and result-independent decrement, immediate-previous-failure bonus, two separate Build stages/destinations, associated Army, unsplit Tax/unrest and stop conditions are resolved.

grades.question: If Company revenue cannot cover expenses, how do emergency loans work at and below max Debt, how does Standing change, and when are expectations and dividends checked?
grades.expected_answer: Expenses £1 per current Debt, officer/regiment excluding Commander, ship in sea zones including China. Emergency loans +£5 each, advance Debt if possible even at maximum continue borrowing; added Debt costs no current-turn interest, then Balance zero. 1–2 emergency loans Standing -1; 3+ -2. Then compare Balance with expectations at current Standing, if below Standing -1. Then optional dividends £1 per share incl Chairman; total dividend payout strictly greater than expectations advances Standing once. Immediate failure when Standing reaches failure.
grades.observed_answer: During Company Revenue expenses, reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer and regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, increasing Debt one at a time to the track end and continuing to receive loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans reduce Standing one; three or more reduce it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under the current Standing; if it is below expectations, reduce Standing one. After this expectations check, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, at £1 per Company share, paying each owner £1 per share including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, Standing advances one. If Standing reaches its leftmost space, the Company fails; during Revenue go immediately to Final Scoring.
grades.reason: Loan amount/track-cap/no-current-turn-interest, zero Balance, Standing loan bands, current expectations next, optional dividends and strict enthusiasm inequality are supplied; unasked expense/dividend formulas are not required.

grades.question: When Company regions face a Crisis, which regions are attacked, in what order and at what strength? How is defense mounted and what happens on successful defense?
grades.expected_answer: Resolve primary first then all other Company regions with unrest, Bombay/Madras/Bengal Army order; each Commander orders own regions. Primary normal invasion/rebellion strength + local unrest, secondary unrest only. Exhaust newly active Army strength equal attack or as much as possible; insufficient means Region Loss. Successful defense clears unrest and Commander gains trophy. Vacant Commander replaced by Military Affairs then Chairman, acting substitute gains/loses no trophies. Additionally, if the primary Crisis was a normal Invasion which failed against the Company, remove one tower level from the attacker if possible.
grades.observed_answer: During a Crisis, resolve the attack at the Elephant's location, with its tail as attacker and head as target; the Event procedure then calls for the Elephant's March. If the attack is against a Company region, it also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary attacks by Presidency order Bombay, Madras, Bengal, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Invasion/Rebellion against the Company has its normal attack strength plus unrest in the target; a Foreign Invasion primary uses only the ordinary attack die, without added unrest. A secondary Rebellion uses only that region's number of unrest cubes, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength or as much as possible, using alliances at printed strength and not splitting them. If newly exhausted defense is insufficient, perform Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in that region and give the Commander one trophy; if that successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses pieces and gains or loses no trophies. This does not appoint a Commander. The summary describes ordering and strengths for attacks on Company regions; ordinary Crisis attack outcomes are: Invasion succeeds only if attacker's whole empire strength plus modifier is greater than defender's whole empire strength; Rebellion compares only the rebelling region's strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital and must be strictly greater. A failed Invasion removes one attacker tower; a failed Rebellion removes one tower from the capital.
grades.summary_evidence: Events in India — Crisis; Attacks on Company; Invasion Crisis; Rebellion Crisis
grades.source_references: Rules p33; lines 2262–2296; Rules p33 lines2290–2296
grades.reason: Historical frozen key: primary-first and Presidency/Commander order, unrest-only secondaries, primary strength, compulsory defense and vacant substitutes, trophy/unrest cleanup and failed-primary-Invasion attacker tower loss are supplied. Subsequent source-gap discovery invalidates any complete core signoff for excess alliance strength.
grades.source_completeness_warning: Historical key did not settle an indivisible alliance exceeding attack strength. Correct means recovery of the historical asked/known procedure only; no definitive overshoot ruling or complete core PASS.

grades.question: What happens when a law fails versus passes, including support-zero, policy movement, Prime Minister and effect order?
grades.expected_answer: Support -1 or lower fails; discard and resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader returns marker and becomes PM, moves selected policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. Zero or higher passes: law with passed laws, PM gains token, selected policy consequence then immediate law effects. Restore vote cards. If legislation fails Company, finish vote then final scoring.
grades.observed_answer: The PM selects a law and a matching policy and sets Vote marker to its printed starting support. Voting begins with the PM and proceeds clockwise; players spend £1 family cash per vote and may add printed card votes. The PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes ends voting. Players may switch from support to opposition, but once opposing they cannot support during that vote. Opposition votes determine the Opposition Leader, with the current holder retaining a tie; votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose with that person's consent. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except under the forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise. At support −1 or less the law fails: discard it, resolve a dilemma's failure text if applicable, Opposition Leader takes the PM dial, and the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher the law passes: place it among passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then the law's immediate effects. After either result, restore every voting card to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
grades.reason: Negative failure versus zero-or-positive passage, law/dilemma handling, PM transfer/adjacent policy, policy-before-immediate-law order, vote-card restoration and finish-vote failure timing are supplied.

grades.question: When can or must a Deregulation session be called in the relevant scenarios, and what are its success/failure effects and exceptions from ordinary voting?
grades.expected_answer: 1758/Long1710 start-turn before London: PM may if Standing and/or Debt lined, must if either starred. Pass reduce Debt one per two Debt, Standing to S, PM law token, activate deregulation. Failure raise share VP value up to ±3, law kept, PM stays. No policy and PM may vote against.
grades.observed_answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, with these exceptions and results: if it passes, reduce Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. If it fails, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. There is no policy with this law; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated, so this session is not needed to activate firms there. The ordinary voting procedure supplies the vote threshold and mechanics; the summary does not enumerate any further exceptions beyond those specified.
grades.reason: Correct scenarios/before-London timing, lined/starred triggers, both outcomes, share-value cap and all special voting exceptions are resolved.

grades.question: How can a firm be formed or invested in, where does money come from, and what restrictions apply to Company shares, invested workshops and the ten-share limit?
grades.expected_answer: Nonmanager forms by returning eligible Company share or flipping workshop invested; flip own board, create family firm share, value leftmost, £5 bank to London. Later investment manager consent, same share/workshop payment gives £5 London and new share. Weak Company share when Standing/Debt lined prohibited; same-turn share prohibited even traded; Chairman piece unavailable. Invested workshop no bonus/failure VP. Ten-share cap but investments continue without new shares.
grades.observed_answer: In a deregulated Firms phase, after Family share creation and before Hiring, investments may be made in any order until nobody wants more; the manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm and the PM resolves conflicts between firms, then managers choose strategies. A player who currently manages no firm may form one by returning one eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to its invested side, flipping their family board, placing a family member as the first firm share, setting Value to the leftmost track space, and taking £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm requires manager consent and the same contribution of a Company share or workshop; it creates a firm share and puts £5 bank money into London. The ten-share maximum applies: investments beyond ten still contribute £5 but create no share. A Chairman share cannot be used; no Company share can be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; and a Company share created this turn cannot be invested even if traded away. Invested workshops never revert, provide no bonus, and give no Company-failure VP, even if the firm fails. The ten-share cap applies to actual firm shares; excess contributions at the cap still add money. The firm money comes from the bank through the specified form/invest procedure, not family cash; family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
grades.summary_evidence: Firms phase: investments; cash location; ten-share limit
grades.reason: Nonmanager formation and manager-consented investment, eligible share/workshop contributions and £5 bank-to-London funds, initial share/value, weak/immature/Chairman restrictions and permanent workshop/ten-share effects are supplied.

grades.question: Explain firm trading strategy, when checks and order filling occur, initiative, capacity, repeat-filled revenue and firm value growth.
grades.expected_answer: After investments managers secretly choose home/sea zone and London cash bid; need ship, may choose even closed home. Reveal cash but not strategy. At associated Presidency start reveal/check once with bid dice, pay bank. Success initiative ships minus number of 1/2 dice; President successful Trade gets same calculation. Fill lowest initiative first, President breaks ties; absent/nontrading President wait for Commander/Governors and Chairman breaks ties. Firm fills max ships+1 open connected orders from chosen home once each; prior-fill by others allowed for half listed value rounded down. Revenue India, advance value one space per £6 revenue this turn. Company may also fill orders previously filled by firms this turn at half listed value, rounded down, retaining normal President and writer bonuses.
grades.observed_answer: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose a trade zone/home port or Hobnob. A trade strategy requires at least one ship, permits a closed home port at selection, and commits a secret cash bid from London treasury; Hobnob has no bid, trade, or dividends, still pays expenses, and retains the previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously but keep strategy cards facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before any actions, reveal matching strategies, roll one die per committed £1, and pay the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), potentially negative. A President that succeeds at Trade gets initiative calculated the same way using Presidency ships. After that success, fill in ascending initiative order; the President chooses the order among ties, with no automatic Company priority. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders and Governors have had their opportunity, and the Chairman chooses initiative ties. Each firm fills as many open orders as possible, up to ships plus one, starting at its strategy home port and tracing through its own filled route back there. It may fill each particular order only once, but can refill orders the Company or another firm filled that turn, and the Company may refill firm-filled orders. Place filled tokens and put trade revenue in India treasury. Any previously filled order pays half its printed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space for every full £6 added to its India treasury this turn.
grades.source_references: Rules p40; lines 2773–2822; Rules p40 lines2817–2820; p41 example
grades.reason: Secret strategy and public-bid/private-card timing, closed-home and single-attempt constraints, check/payment and initiative, both tie authorities/timing, ships-plus-one route and one fill per order, reciprocal half-revenue refills and £6 India-based value growth are resolved.

grades.question: How are firm expenses and dividends funded and calculated, and what happens to a failing firm, its shares and workshops?
grades.expected_answer: Start Revenue firms act initiative order then others, ties manager windows then PM clockwise. Expenses £1 per ship plus max(shares, firm value); either treasury. If cannot pay dissolution (or emergency rescue): shares Debtors Prison -1 VP each, ships shipyards, charter family, invested workshops stay invested. Dividends only India, £1 per share plus £1 manager each; shareholder may forgo with manager consent. Record total paid retirement marker then sweep remainder India to London.
grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, before Company expenses, firms pay in initiative order and then other firms; ties go to the manager with most windows and then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of firm share count or firm Value, and may be paid from either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, the firm dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends its shares to Debtor's Prison (each costs −1 VP), returns ships to shipyards and the charter to the family side; invested workshops remain invested. It may be rescued by emergency investments following normal Company-share/workshop rules—even if the ten-share limit prevents more shares, the firm still gets the investment money; use it to pay expenses, lose any remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment—or by merging with one other firm. In the latter case, the other firm must first pay its own expenses if it has not already and cover the failing firm's unpaid expenses. After expenses the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend costs £1 per firm share plus £1 for the manager; with manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on a dividend. Record the total actual cash paid out on the Company Balance track as the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep the remaining India money into London. Firm ships face storms in their strategy zone, except Hobnob ships are exempt.
grades.reason: Expense formula and either treasury, India-only per-share/manager dividends and waiver, actual payout marker/cash sweep, failure/rescue and prison/ship/charter/workshop destinations are supplied; unasked inter-firm order details are not required.
